subject: Marketplace visibility and fallback prioritization for AWS/Azure/GCP
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 15:15:00 -0800
Subject: Marketplace visibility and fallback prioritization for AWS/Azure/GCP

Team —

We have three parallel partner asks coming in for listing variants and co-sell enablement. I pulled a draft visibility matrix (attached) and sketched three possible priorities; I want to pick one approach by EOD Friday so we can push the co-sell intake to the partners next week. High-level options:

1) Single flagship SKU everywhere (simple, fastest co-sell enablement, risks mismatch to region price/latency needs)
2) Cloud-specific SKUs (tune packaging + quotas per cloud/region; more operational overhead, better fit for enterprise procurement)
3) Hybrid: flagship SKU + 1 cloud-optimized SKU (AWS priority first, then Azure, GCP later)

Key constraints:
- GCP will not accept multi-tenant SKUs that aggregate reserved vs. on-demand pricing; they want per-instance SKU metadata.
- Azure co-sell has a stricter submission checklist (Marissa, you have a note on docs needed).
- AWS is our biggest channel for inbound trials (Ben: we need to decide whether to gate regions EMEA/APAC for the initial listing).

Please review the attached visibility matrix (redwood_marketplace_visibility_matrix_v2.xlsx) and reply with: 1) your recommended option (1/2/3), 2) any blockers (legal/tech/finance), and 3) which regions we should mark as "visible" vs "canary" per cloud.

Attachments: redwood_marketplace_visibility_matrix_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet), co-sell-readiness-checklist.pdf (doc stub)

Thanks —
Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Head of GTM Partnerships | Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 17:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Marketplace visibility and fallback prioritization for AWS/Azure/GCP

Jasmine —

Thanks for the tidy deck. My quick read: Option 3 (Hybrid) gives us the best tradeoff between speed and control. Concrete recommendations below:

- AWS: flagship SKU + AWS-optimized SKU. Make US (all regions) visible, EMEA as canary (start with eu-west-1 + eu-central-1), and APAC limited to ap-northeast-1 for now. Reason: our Dedicated capacity in EMEA/APAC is still ramping and we should avoid SLA surprises.
- Azure: flagship SKU only for initial listing. Azure requires additional docs for co-sell; Marissa and Lauren to finalize the readiness checklist. Mark visible: US East + West, canary: UK South.
- GCP: keep as flagship with explicit instance metadata. GCP marketplace tends to be stricter on billing semantics; do not launch GCP-optimized SKU yet. Visible: us-central1 only as pilot.

Blockers: legal wants a short addendum for the reseller terms if we create cloud-specific SKUs (Ben, can you sync with Finance on margin impact?). Also confirm that our deployment template can emit per-cloud usage metadata for GCP.

I agree with Ben that we should allow fallback routing by region + cloud: if AWS capacity is saturated, route to AWS cheaper variant (if available) then fallback to the flagship Hosted API in a secondary region. The matrix shows a recommended fallback order — I'll update with latency targets if folks want.

Karthik
Director, Cloud GTM

From: Sara Kim <sara.kim@microsoft.com>

Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 09:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace visibility and fallback prioritization for AWS/Azure/GCP

Hi Jasmine / Marissa —

Thanks for the overview. A few clarifying points from the Azure marketplace side that will affect packaging decisions:

- Co-sell approval requires an enablement packet (whitepaper + 3 customer references + usage-based pricing table). The checklist you attached is a good start, but we need references that reflect regional deployments (especially EU).
- If you create a cloud-specific SKU labelled "Azure-optimized," it must map to the Azure IaaS types and include an offer ID per region — that increases the listing effort by ~1.5x.
- For fallback, Azure prefers that customers see a single offer in the portal and that the backend performs routing; multiple visible offers can confuse the co-sell team. If you want both visibility and a cloud-optimized SKU, consider using an "offer alias" approach where the flagship offer is primary and the cloud-optimized SKU is an internal variant.

Questions:
1) Do you have the three EU references Marissa noted?
2) Can you confirm whether the Azure-optimized SKU will include the same terms (refunds, retention) as the flagship?

If you want, we can slot a 30-min call with Azure co-sell ops next Tue to walk through the submission template.

—Sara
Sara Kim
Partner Program Manager, Microsoft Marketplace

Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 10:10:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Marketplace visibility and fallback prioritization for AWS/Azure/GCP — decision and next steps

Quick summary and decisions:

- Approach chosen: Option 3 (Hybrid). We will publish a single flagship offer across all three clouds and add an AWS-optimized SKU for improved pricing/throughput in AWS regions. No public Azure-optimized or GCP-optimized SKUs at launch.
- Regions: AWS visible: us-east-1/us-west-2; EMEA canary: eu-west-1; APAC pilot: ap-northeast-1. Azure visible: eastus/westus; UK South canary. GCP pilot: us-central1 only.
- Fallback policy: route requests first to same-cloud optimized variant (if present), then to flagship in same region cluster, then to cross-cloud flagship in secondary region (latency guardrail 300ms). Karthik to codify routing priorities in the matrix.
- Attachments & readiness: Marissa to collect 3 EU references and finalize the co-sell-readiness-checklist.pdf by Monday. Ben to check reseller term impact with Finance and confirm margin delta by Wednesday.
- External ops: Sara — we will take the 30-min call Tuesday; please propose times. I copied AWS/GCP so partner ops teams are aware of the plan.

Next steps (owners + due dates):
- Marissa: finalize checklist + references (2026-11-16)
- Ben: reseller term and finance check (2026-11-18)
- Karthik: update matrix with routing fallback and latency targets + push to Drive (2026-11-13)
- Jasmine: prepare partner submission packet and coordinate co-sell call slots (2026-11-15)

Thanks everyone — goal is to submit initial offers to AWS/Azure by 11/20 and GCP pilot shortly after.

Jasmine
Head of GTM Partnerships | Redwood Inference
